conflict_topics: strong-smelling cooking (fish curry) affecting shared spaces
laundry absorbing cooking smells in service yard
video call disruption from cooking smells
scheduling use of the shared kitchen
dialogue_quality_notes: Agents consistently referenced relevant facts (call times, laundry days) and used them to negotiate concrete trade-offs.
Agent D's cultural justification: 'that's the food I grew up with.' framed initial resistance before proposing a schedule.
Agent C repeated schedule once ('I just said. Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays in the evening.'), indicating mild frustration/repetition.
Clear, concrete closing lines that implemented the compromise: 'Tuesdays and Thursdays after 7.'
evaluation.final_reason: Housemates reached a concrete schedule and mutual accommodations: Agent D agreed to limit curry cooking to Tuesdays and Thursdays (Agent D: 'Then how about I cook my curry on Tuesdays and Thursdays?'); Agent C accepted that schedule ('Okay, that works.'); Agent A added a timing constraint to protect calls ('Okay, so Tuesdays and Thursdays after 7. That works for me.'); Agent B will be notified and close their door when cooking occurs ('If you just let me know before you start, I can close my door.'). These spoken, mutual acceptances settled the outstanding incompatibilities.
position_change_notes: Agent D moved from initial defense ('that's the food I grew up with') to an explicit compromise proposal ('I cook my curry on Tuesdays and Thursdays').
Agent C shifted from complaint about laundry smell to acceptance of D's proposed schedule ('Okay, that works').
Agent A softened from requesting no strong-smelling food 'from now on' to accepting a timed compromise ('Tuesdays and Thursdays after 7').
Agent B accepted a pragmatic accommodation (will close door if notified) rather than blocking cooking entirely.

substantive_insights: Core tension was between cultural food practices and the shared-flat practical costs (smell affecting work and laundry).
Scheduling and timing are effective low-cost mitigations in a context where no one wants to pay for physical changes.
Resolution relied on trade-offs: D retained ability to cook some days while others adjusted routines (laundry timing, closing doors).
Concrete mutual commitments (who cooks when; who will notify; when laundry is done) are what converted complaints into a stable agreement.
